title: LLM cost & latency reading sprint — notes and small experiments
summary: Scratchpad for a short reading sprint focused on token-level cost/latency tradeoffs, KV-cache compression ideas, and pragmatic microbenchmarks to bring into Redwood Optimize and serving-runtime experiments.
content:
Context / goal:
- 3-day reading sprint while waiting on infra quota increase. Primary focus: practical wins we can test quickly in serving-runtime and Redwood Optimize (eg batching knobs, cheap quant profiles, KV compression).
- Not a polished doc; notes to self + next steps for quick experiments to validate hypotheses.

High-level takeaways (quick):
- Small changes often beat fancy algos: prompt token trimming, better two-stage routing to cheaper model variants, and per-customer prefix caching show immediate cost wins.
- KV-cache compression seems promising at 1.5–2x memory savings with low decode overhead if we work in block-compressed representation (paper notes below). Integration risk: GPU-friendly layout is key.
- Quantization-aware perf wins are workload dependent: 4-bit with outlier handling gave best cost/latency tradeoff on our medium-length chat traces; but hallucination/regression risk increases for retrieval-augmented tasks. Need targeted evals.

Papers / blog notes (own words + quick critiques):
1) "BlockKV: Compact Key-Value Stores for Long-context LMs" (arXiv 2029) — gist: store KV cache in fixed-size compressed blocks, use LZ-like entropy coding per block + small per-block bloom filter to skip decompression if not needed.
   - Why it matters: aligns with prefix caching + long context, lowers GPU memory pressure so we can increase batch sizes or shard KV across fewer GPUs.
   - Implementation note: the per-block bloom dramatically reduces decompress work at short sequence lengths — good fit for our mixed chat/query workloads.
   - Questions: how to layout blocks in CUDA-friendly way? decompress in CPU thread pool vs on-device kernel? latency tradeoff for single-token generation needs microbench.

2) "QuantMix: Outlier-aware 4-bit Quantization for LLMs" (ICLR 2030 poster + code) — gist: handle outlier weights by keeping small 16-bit outlier table + 4-bit main storage. Simple reconstructions perform well.
   - Takeaway: on many open models, QuantMix (4-bit + outlier) preserves perplexity while reducing memory >2x and inference latency slightly improves with smaller memory bandwidth.
   - Redwood implication: could be a candidate profile in Optimize. Need to pair with per-route quality checks (evals).

3) "Prompt Budgeting: token-aware routing for cost containment" — recent blog by startup X, practical recipe more than research.
   - Idea: route short prompts to cheaper small models, or to cached prefix matches; chargeback at token-level and provide early termination heuristics.
   - Practical: implement as per-route policy in routing layer; baseline metric: fraction of requests routed to cheaper tier without impact on user metrics.

Quick microbench ideas (order by cheapest-to-run):
- A: Token trimming experiment (day 1): run simulation over 7k chat requests from prod sample. Compare naive trim (drop trailing whitespace & stop tokens) vs smart trim (strip repeated system text snippets) 
   - Metrics: token-savings, generation latency, failure rate (completions truncated mid-sentence), and end-to-end cost delta.
- B: KV-block read microbench (day 2): implement a CPU-based prototype of block-compressed KV cache on a small trace (1000 sessions). Measure per-step latency overhead and hit/decompress ratio.
   - If CPU overhead < 0.4ms median on our machines, consider porting lightweight decompress to CUDA kernels.
- C: QuantMix inference run (day 3): pick a 7B and a 13B open model, apply QuantMix pipeline from paper, run throughput + latency vs native FP16 and current 8-bit profile. Also run embeddings/regression suite to check quality regression.
- D: Two-stage routing A/B (week): implement routing rule in local dev that sends to cheap-medium-expensive chain with fallbacks. Run synthetic workload with varying prompt lengths to measure cost/latency and fallback incidence.

Short experiment playbook (notes to self):
- Use the small trace in s3://redwood-experiments/mini-traces/June2031/ (ask Ethan for access) to avoid prod risk.
- Make each microbench configurable: seed, concurrency, max-gen-length, temperature. Log token counts and per-request breakdown.
- Baseline everything with current serving-runtime profile (q8_main) and recorded latency distribution for comparison.

Open questions / risks to surface early:
- For block-KV: latency cliff when a request needs many blocks — need to detect and fall back to uncompressed KV path gracefully.
- For QuantMix: which layers must be exempt from quantization to avoid QA regressions (decoder output layers? Layernorms?). Need layer-sensitivity sweep.
- For routing: how to roll out without causing an observability gap. We should surface per-request score/decision in Console traces.

Concrete next actions (short):
- Today: automated token-trim simulation + small script to estimate token-cost delta (Marta).
- Tomorrow: spike CPU block-KV prototype (Marta + Ethan), repo: github/dev/mrueda/kv-block-spike, push WIP PR and link to INF-4923.
- End of week: QuantMix script on 7B model (Hannah volunteered to help with conversion pipeline).

Notes-to-self / rough commands:
- local trace loader: python tools/trace_playback.py --trace s3://redwood-experiments/mini-traces/June2031/chat_sample.json --seed 42 --concurrency 16 --max-gen 256 --profile q8_main
- kv-block prototype: pin block_size=8192, use zstd -1 for compress, bloom_bits=10 per block. If decompress-ms > 0.5ms median, try threading to overlap with token decode.

Useful links and references (captured while reading):
- BlockKV paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/xxxx.xxxxx (save copy to confluence)
- QuantMix repo: https://github.com/quantmix/quantmix (code does small outlier table export)
- Prompt budgeting blog: https://startupx.blog/prompt-budgeting-2029
- Slack thread: #infra-kv-cache (pinned message, see link in Console)

Random heuristics & heuristics to try later:
- Keep the first n=120 tokens of user context untrimmed, but aggressively trim repeated system prompts after that. This tends to keep intent while saving tokens.
- If KV-hit_rate < 0.05 for a session, skip block-decompress path and use lightweight no-cache mode (less mem, simpler).

TODOs (bullet):
- [ ] Push token-trim sim results to confluence page and tag product-hosted-api for feedback.
- [ ] Create initial kv-block prototype PR and request SLO review with SRE.
- [ ] Run QuantMix on 7B and 13B and produce small metrics table (tokens/sec, median latency, eval-quality delta).
- [ ] Add per-request routing decision to Console traces for any routing A/B tests.

Log of quick decisions while reading:
- Dropped trying on-device compression for now; start with CPU decompress + async overlap. If we see CPU bottleneck, revisit kernel work.
- Prioritize token-trim & routing since both are config-only and lower risk.

End notes:
- This sprint is intentionally shallow but broad — goal is to surface 2 safe experiments we can ship as Optimize suggestions or serving-runtime toggles by Q3.
- Revisit after experiments: pick 1 deep project (likely KV-block with CUDA kernel) to prototype as a proper feature.

-- marta
(Notes left informal; will tidy later if something gains traction.)
